 8:24AM
 How England have fared since 2019
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Some poor years in there, certainly, but results are on the up in 2026. 
 8:10AM
 Good morning
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Welcome to our coverage for England’s first match in the tri-series between Pakistan, Sri Lanka and England in Rawalpindi. Series like this have gone out of fashion in the last couple of decades, so it is nice to see them return. Pakistan and Sri Lanka have already played their first match in this tournament, with Pakistan running out winners by 37 runs, having been bowled out for 305 after 39.5 overs. 
 England’s fixtures are as follows: 
 October 20 - Pakistan, 9am (Rawalpindi)
 October 22 - Sri Lanka, 9am (Rawalpindi)
 October 25 - Pakistan, 8am (Lahore)
 October 29 - Sri Lanka, 8am (Lahore) 
 And if they amass enough points from those group-stage games to finish in the top two then they will make the final in Lahore on Saturday, October 31 in Lahore. 
 It has been a funny few years for England in the one-day international realm. Certainly there has been plenty of disappointment and difficult results after the 2019 World Cup triumph. In some ways that was to be expected, success is hard to maintain an England reached a previously unreached peak seven years ago. Still, there seemed to be little direction. 
 Things have been improved in recent times with England winning all three of their three-match series so far this year 2-1. The World Cup starts in around a year, so these types of tournaments are good ground for England to find their best team and squad with the aim of regaining the trophy. Harry Brook’s team also have a tour to Australia in this format coming up. 
 This match starts at 9am and we will be here for the toss, team news and all the updates from a potential 100 overs.
